name: Ashokan Brahmi
diagnosticFeatures: Strictly rectilinear and geometric strokes
Total absence of top headmark (Talakattu)
Basic geometric circle, cross, and vertical bar foundations
Uniform stroke width without calligraphic modulation
significance: First attested written records in Karnataka, marking the foundational root of Indian epigraphy.

sampleGlyphs.label: Foundation Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Rectilinear glyph formed by a vertical spine and two leftward angled arms.

sampleGlyphs.label: Unaspirated Velar Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Symmetrical orthogonal cross (+) chiseled deeply into coarse granite.

sampleGlyphs.label: Voiced Velar Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Inverted chevron (^) representing voiced stop without horizontal base closure.

name: Satavahana Brahmi
diagnosticFeatures: Emergence of base curvatures on vertical stems
Incipient triangular thickening or serif at stem tops
Curved horizontal vowel diacritics (Matras)
Modulated chisel pressure visible on limestone
significance: Bridge between North Indian Mauryan Brahmi and regional Dravidian epigraphical traditions.

sampleGlyphs.label: Initial Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Beginnings of curvature on lower left hook with upper serif thickening.

sampleGlyphs.label: Velar Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Crossbar exhibits slight curve with terminal chisel indentation.

sampleGlyphs.label: Voiced Velar
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Rounded arch replacing the sharp angle of Mauryan Brahmi.

name: Kadamba (Proto-Kannada)
diagnosticFeatures: Diagnostic box-headed top bar (Petika-shirsha)
Curving loops at base of consonants like ka, ra, and ma
Early formal separation of Kannada-Telugu branch
Emergence of archaic phonemes: Sakata Repha (ಱ) and Kula Repha (ೞ)
significance: Birth of formal Kannada epigraphy, marked by the iconic Halmidi inscription (c. 450 CE).

sampleGlyphs.label: Box-Headed Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Distinct square hollow box (Petika-shirsha) crowning the central stem.

sampleGlyphs.label: Proto-Kannada Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Looping base curve with square box-head incision at top.

sampleGlyphs.label: Curved Base Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: U-shaped rounded horseshoe arch with square terminal caps.

name: Badami Chalukya
diagnosticFeatures: Morphing of box-head into a hooked horizontal bar
Pronounced inner loops in ba, bha, ya, and ma
Upward sweeping arched vowel canopies
Bilateral symmetry with elegant vertical tails
significance: Golden age of monumental cliff epigraphs (Aihole, Badami, Mahakuta).

sampleGlyphs.label: Early Old Kannada Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Hooked horizontal bar replacing the box-head with sweeping side arcs.

sampleGlyphs.label: Looped Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Full loop formation at the bottom with open hooked crown.

sampleGlyphs.label: Curved Velar
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Balanced bilateral arch with subtle terminal flourish.

name: Rashtrakuta
diagnosticFeatures: Horizontally broadened and vertically compressed glyph proportion
Stabilization of curved top hook into a mature proto-talakattu
Clear vertical stacking of subjoined consonants (Vattakshara)
Standardized copper-plate charter script form
significance: Era of Kavirajamarga (c. 850 CE); definitive flourishing of Classical Old Kannada (Halegannada).

sampleGlyphs.label: Classical Old Kannada Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Horizontally compressed proportions with pronounced proto-talakattu.

sampleGlyphs.label: Broadened Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Flared side arms and structured lower loop.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standardized Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Arched glyph with stabilized top incision and flat base balance.

name: Kalyana Chalukya
diagnosticFeatures: Exquisite circular calligraphic contours enabled by chloritic schist
Flared terminal strokes and intricate circular vowel loops
Arched notch headmarks
Refined geometric balance across 50 characters
significance: Introduction of fine-grained soapstone carving created the most circular phase of Kannada script.

sampleGlyphs.label: Soapstone Circular Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: High circularity with delicate curved vowel loops chiseled in schist.

sampleGlyphs.label: Swirling Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Spiral inner contours and distinct notched headmark.

sampleGlyphs.label: Curved Plosive
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Circular arc with refined terminal serif.

name: Hoysala
diagnosticFeatures: Maximum artistic floridity with double-loops and cursive finials
Standardized check-mark / V-shaped downward Talakattu
Multi-tier stacked consonant ligatures with decorative curls
Dense inscriptional layout with micro-sculpted relief
significance: Considered the peak artistic achievement of South Indian stone calligraphy.

sampleGlyphs.label: Ornate Florid Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Double curls and decorative tail terminating in calligraphic flourish.

sampleGlyphs.label: Sculpted Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Intricate loop-in-loop structure with pronounced V-shaped Talakattu.

sampleGlyphs.label: Flowing Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Curving arch adorned with upper notch and downward ligature cusp.

name: Vijayanagara
diagnosticFeatures: Functional simplification adapted to hard granite substrates
Definitive morphological divergence between Kannada and Telugu scripts
Standardized uniform kerning with isolated glyph bodies
Clear, bold stroke architecture with pronounced T-bar
significance: Pre-modern administrative script spanning monumental temple steles across South India.

sampleGlyphs.label: Granite-Carved Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Bold, robust circular loop designed to endure hard granite chiseling.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standardized Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Isolated glyph body with clear horizontal T-bar and rounded base.

sampleGlyphs.label: Open Horseshoe Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Even-thickness arch resembling modern Kannada letter architecture.

name: Mysuru Wodeyar
diagnosticFeatures: Fluid cursive arcs influenced by iron-stylus palm leaf writing
Modern open-circle body shapes for ka, ra, la, da
Systematic detached lower subscript conjuncts
Direct prototype for 19th-century metal type typography
significance: Crucial transitional bridge from manuscript traditions to modern print culture.

sampleGlyphs.label: Manuscript Cursive Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Smooth circular sweep designed not to tear dried palm leaves.

sampleGlyphs.label: Pre-Print Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Direct precursor to 19th-century Basel Mission metal type.

sampleGlyphs.label: Modern-Contour Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Near-identical geometry to contemporary Kannada letter forms.

name: Present Kannada
diagnosticFeatures: Standardized 49-53 character Varnamale
Consistent open check-mark Talakattu (✓)
Standard typographic grid with normalized kerning and baselines
Unicode standard encoding (U+0C80 to U+0CFF)
significance: Standardized modern literary and administrative script of Karnataka.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standardized Unicode Vowel
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Normalized baseline, uniform stroke modulation, standard open loop.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standard Typographic Consonant
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Standard check-mark talakattu (✓) with calibrated inner kerning.

sampleGlyphs.label: Standard Typographic Arch
sampleGlyphs.morphologicalNote: Balanced arch with standard open top talakattu mark.
